text.p: Italian debt markets started on a higher note but soon succumbed to profit-taking reflecting a lower close to T-bonds overnight and moves to consolidate after hitting fresh record highs on Wednesday, dealers said.

They added that sentiment for BTPs was still positive but that today will likely see a phase of consolidation after the market digested the second leg of Federal Reserve's chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
"There were no fireworks from the second leg of Greenspan's speech so the market will look to consolidate after Wednesday's sharp rise," one LIFFE dealer said.
Dealers said that both BTP futures and the bund spread could reach new records in coming weeks with optimism continuing over Italy making the first wave of members to join Europe's single currency.
